findings.message: `stored()` turns every `SecretsUnavailableError` into NO_KEY_SERVICE ("no key service is set (AMAX_KMS); an operator sets it"). `REFUSALS` in modules/git-accounts/server/app.ts:9 does the same. But `dataKeyFor` (packages/core/src/secrets/runtime.ts:37-39) throws that same error class for three other reasons: the tenant has no data key yet, the tenant's data key was destroyed when it left amax (034), and the key is held by a different KMS than AMAX_KMS. In those three cases the AC-6 fix tells the Admin something false and points them at the wrong fix. The fix only covers the case it was named for (AMAX_KMS unset). Fix: send NO_KEY_SERVICE only when no KMS is configured. That check could be `kmsLabel() === null`, or a distinct reason or subclass on the error. For the other causes, pass the error's own reason through. Add a table test that covers no KMS, a mismatched KMS and a destroyed data key, in both put_secret and set_github_app.
findings.scenario: The tenant's data_key row has kms='aws' and the deployment has AMAX_KMS=local. An Admin confirms set_github_app (or put_secret). The refusal reads "no key service is set (AMAX_KMS); an operator sets it", but AMAX_KMS is set. The real problem is a KMS mismatch, and the message hides it.

findings.message: The "Rotate the GitHub app secret" suggestion fills in a prompt that the scripted provider (packages/ai/src/scripted.ts) matches with its `rotate the (.+?) (?:token|secret|key)` rule. That rule sends rotate_secret with connector "github-app", which isn't a connector, so the zod enum refuses it. In local demos and e2e runs (AMAX_AI_PROVIDER=scripted), the suggestion fails instead of opening a set_github_app card. The "Remove the GitHub app" prompt doesn't match any scripted rule either, so it falls through to listing projects. Fix: make the scripted provider route these two prompts to set_github_app and revoke_secret (github-oauth), or reword the prompts so they match the rules it already has.
findings.scenario: With AMAX_AI_PROVIDER=scripted, an Admin on /settings/integrations clicks "Rotate the GitHub app secret". Chat calls rotate_secret{connector:"github-app"}, which fails with an invalid input error, and no card appears.

findings.message: AC-6's callback-URL refusal only works when GitHub's registered Redirect URI already points at amax's callback. GitHub sends `error=redirect_uri_mismatch` to the app's *registered* callback URL. So the 2026-11-16 case the change was written for (the Redirect URI was set to the homepage) lands on `/?error=redirect_uri_mismatch&...`. The callback route never runs, so the person sees nothing and the connect claim stays pending. The token-exchange branch in `readGitHubUser` is only reached after GitHub has already accepted the URI. Fix: check before the connect link goes out, or catch the mismatch where GitHub actually returns. For example, have the Overview/root route recognise `error=redirect_uri_mismatch` with a pending connect state and show `callbackRefused(redirectUri())`. Add a test where the fake GitHub sends the error to a non-callback URL.
findings.scenario: Admin sets the GitHub app's Redirect URI to https://amax.example/ → Kasun confirms Connect GitHub → GitHub redirects to https://amax.example/?error=redirect_uri_mismatch → Overview renders normally, with no message saying the callback URL is wrong.

findings.message: AC-5 says Overview *leads with* the Connect GitHub item. But the nudge's `since` is `new Date()`, and `gatherOverview` sorts waiting items oldest first, so the nudge always sorts last. `WaitingTable` shows only the first 6 items, so anyone with 6 or more pending decisions never sees it. It also always reads "0 h" waiting. Fix: give nudges their own place in the list (for example, sort `snoozeDays` items first or render them above the decisions) instead of borrowing the decision ordering.
findings.scenario: A PM with 7 open suggestions and no GitHub login opens Overview → the table shows the 6 oldest decisions → the Connect GitHub item is cut off behind 'Oldest 6 of 8 shown'.

findings.message: The nudge is not a decision, but it still gets a selection checkbox and is included by 'Select all' and 'Approve selected'. Bulk approve then pins Git accounts and asks chat to 'Approve these N decisions', and that count includes Connect GitHub. Leave items with `snoozeDays` out of selection.
findings.scenario: Select all with 2 suggestions and the nudge → chat gets 'Approve these 3 decisions' with get_my_git_identities pinned.

findings.message: `expiryDayProblem` builds the end-of-day instant itself (`${d}T23:59:59Z`) instead of calling `endOfDay`, which sits next to it. If the day-to-instant rule ever changes in one place, the check and the stored value could disagree. Use `endOfDay(d)`.

`storeGitHubApp` reads the credential row (add or replace, kept expiry, grace) outside `putSecret`'s transaction. If two Admins confirm at once, both can see 'no row' and both run the add path; the second write's outcome then depends on what `putSecret` does with an existing credential. Decide add vs. replace inside the service's transaction.
The page calls the read tool with `source: "chat"`, but the call comes from a server-rendered page, not chat. Any trace or audit attributes it to chat. Pass the page's own source (ui).

fix_proof.reason: no review.test_command configured, so no test could prove the fix
